newsitem.title: INDIA: Large RBI spot dollar buying dents Indian rupee.
newsitem.headline: Large RBI spot dollar buying dents Indian rupee.

text.p: Large-scale dollar buying by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dragged the rupee to close at 35.865/870 against the dollar on Friday, dealers said.
Spot dollar opened Friday at 35.84/85 rupees.
The RBI initiated its intervention in the forward market in the morning session but switched to large-scale spot dollar purchases in the afternoon, dealers said.
They said Friday's intervention was in excess of $150 million.
"They bought from me upto 35.8675 level," said a dealer at a leading foreign bank. He said the RBI was even making enquiries to buy dollars at 35.87 towards the close of trading.
"He kept returning and taking away the surplus dollars," another dealer said, referring to the RBI.
The RBI's intervention was relatively muted in the forwards section but helped push up the premiums.
The six-month annualised forward premium breached the seven percent barrier to close Friday at 7.14 percent, up from the previous close of 6.92 percent, dealers said.
Thursday's RBI intervention in the forward market across wide maturities raised speculation whether the central bank was attempting to depreciate the rupee gradually in phases.

"They are trying to create dollar demand over the next six months aimed at a gradual depreciation of the rupee," Aashish Pitale, manager debt research at ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said.
The chief forex dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay wondered whether preventing the rupee's rise was RBI's only objective.
"It could even be a genuine desire to shore up the reserves for some impending large payment -- maybe oil or debt," he said.
The RBI has has always said its intervention was aimed at keeping the exchange rate in tune with the real effective exchange rate and to avoid sharp volatilities.
